status: Prospective research assumptions for the frozen random split. No candidate results informed these choices. A material change requires a new immutable version, rationale, and registration before use; label retrospective work exploratory.
action: An issued 1 flags a contact; an issued 0 clears it. A deferred row of either true class goes to review with no automated class decision. Review cost represents the assumed total downstream burden; review accuracy, eventual outcome and monetary return are unknown.

cost.loss: (FP_retained + 2*FN_retained + defer*(D_positive+D_negative))/N. Divide by all evaluation rows. Re-score fixed actions at the two sensitivity costs; report reversals without reselecting.
cost.basis: One unnecessary flag is the unit. Missing a subscriber is assumed twice as costly; four reviews consume one unit. Sensitivity spans ten reviews to two per unit. These are research exchange rates, not measured bank costs.

coverage.ranking: Higher finite nonnegative confidence is retained first. Keep whole equal-confidence groups. On the same rows in each outer fold, compare at exactly ceil(g*N) retained for every arm in a comparison. If any arm cannot reach that count, mark the contrast unavailable and report its bracketing counts. Never use an evaluation rank cut for deployment.
coverage.risk: (FP_retained + 2*FN_retained)/N_retained. Record achieved coverage at every distinct confidence. No risk at zero retained.
coverage.aurc: Partial AURC on [0.50,1], divided by 0.50. For each requested minimum coverage u use risk at the smallest attainable coverage >= u: integrate this step function exactly by rectangle widths, clipping the first interval at 0.50. Report each fold and row-weighted mean. This summarizes minimum-coverage obligations; only exact common counts are called matched.
coverage.cut: On pooled cross-fitted inner predictions, enumerate observed confidence cuts (retain >= cut). Represent all-retained by 0. Minimize primary loss subject to total and both true-class retention floors and retained counts. Ties: higher coverage then smaller cut. Across feasible class thresholds minimize loss, then maximize coverage, then use the listed threshold order. If infeasible, record failure; never relax floors or derive a fallback from outer data. Lock the numeric cut for the outer fold.
coverage.basis: Half coverage anchors the historical comparison. The same half-floor for each class prevents sacrificing a majority of either class. Twenty is a minimum reporting/eligibility count, not a precision guarantee. The grid spans limited review through zero review.

report.all: All rows before deferral: TP, FP, TN, FN, PR-AUC on ranking score; log-loss, Brier and 10-bin equal-width ECE only on probability outputs. Show calibration before and after any inner-fitted correction. GLASS weighted ranking score has no probability claim.
report.retained: Report confusion counts, weighted selective risk and descriptive F2=5TP/(5TP+4FN+FP). F2 on retained rows never selects a configuration, weight or cut.
report.whole: Report N, retained/N, deferred/N, loss, effective recall=retained TP/all positives, class retention=retained class/all class, retained prevalence=retained positives/retained. Count deferred positives, deferred negatives, correct decisions deferred and incorrect decisions deferred using the class prediction before deferral.
report.support: Undefined denominator or one-class discrimination: report NA with counts. Report subgroups descriptively; suppress calibration slopes and inferential subgroup contrasts below 20 observations of either class. Missing support for a required safeguard makes promotion inconclusive.

comparisons.design: Within each upstream compare linear vs formula and linear vs Meta-XGBoost on identical rows. Formula is the GLASS native reference; Meta-XGBoost is the black-box native reference. Primary comparators are the fold-refitted accepted formula and the inner-selected Meta procedure. Formula improvements and fixed-vs-tuned Meta contrasts are secondary and cannot replace the primary formula reference. Preserve the historical PR 39 2x2 as a separate reproduction. Common-policy arms use their own fitting rules and one registered decision policy.
comparisons.channels: Only Stage 1/3 probabilities, routed Stage 2 transformed probability, and route indicators; missing router probability on deferral. Formula and linear may re-express these using producer base rates as frozen provenance and training-fitted cuts. No extra row features, rule identifiers or label-derived side channels. Cross-fitted rule precision is a separate evidence ablation on common inputs if available to every comparator.
comparisons.selection_order: Generate model scores, learn eligible probability calibration, form the all-row class decision, compute confidence, then select deferral. Use cross-fitted inner probabilities for every downstream selection, including calibration. Between eligible variants select smallest inner loss; ties prefer fewer free parameters, then registered enumeration order. Lock all choices before outer scoring.

uncertainty.method: Candidate minus reference per-row realized loss. Percentile interval of paired mean differences; resample rows with replacement within outer-fold by true-class strata at their observed sizes. Reuse stage1_calibration.evidence.stratified_bootstrap_delta with identical seed, row order and strata for all contrasts. Bonferroni two-sided 98.75% intervals for the four predeclared loss contrasts; descriptive 95% intervals elsewhere. No promotion by secondary contrast. Report all five fold differences and sample SD.
uncertainty.limits: Conditional on the rows, prevalence, fitted OOF streams and chosen outer models. Does not measure upstream refit or time drift; folds share training rows. Coefficient intervals are descriptive: 500 paired stratified training-row bootstrap refits of the selected linear form, fixed preprocessing and penalty, seed 4303; report 2.5/97.5 percentiles and outer-fold coefficients.

decision.basis: 0.005 loss is five false-flag equivalents per thousand contacts. Use the same tolerance for coverage-averaged retained loss. Two percentage points limits differential class exclusion; 0.005 Brier limits extra mean squared probability error. ECE 0.05 uses the existing Stage 3 calibration gate scale. These prospective tolerances are design judgments.
decision.loss_verdict: Improved if interval upper < -improvement AND absolute mean gain exceeds sample SD of the five fold differences. Comparable only if entire interval is within +/-comparability. Materially worse if lower > comparability. Otherwise inconclusive.
decision.safeguards: At locked cuts require all outer folds to satisfy the absolute coverage/support floors. On pooled issued actions require neither class retention to drop by more than max_retention_drop vs the comparator. For linear promotion vs the accepted formula additionally require both pooled retention differences >= 0. Require pooled calibrated-probability ECE <= max_ece and Brier <= same-upstream Stage 1 Brier + max_brier_increase, and when comparator has probabilities also <= comparator Brier + max_brier_increase. Ranking-only formula is exempt from probability gates and cannot be preferred for probability use. Require partial AURC increase <= max_aurc_increase and report matched grid gaps.
decision.disposition: Assess per upstream. Advance linear only with improvement over the accepted formula and improvement or comparability vs Meta-XGBoost plus safeguards. Retain the accepted formula on a formula/linear tie. Prefer an interpretable qualifying arm to a comparable nonlinear arm. Require an auditable additive contribution and route trace for each GLASS decision, nonnegative voter slopes for linear, and recorded fit time within its registered budget. Hard safeguard failure or material loss rejects promotion; uncertainty, unavailable evidence, convergence or budget failure leaves an inconclusive candidate. No pooled winner across upstreams.

search.common: Budgets per upstream and outer training partition. Fresh fits, seed 42, single-thread deterministic search and fixed trial order. No early success stopping. Failed trials count; skip nonconverged fits and log cause. Exhaust the cap or finite list; no grid enlargement. Historical frozen cuts remain descriptive. On probability outputs compare class thresholds 0.10, 0.20, 1/3, 0.50 (1/3 is the calibrated Bayes threshold for 1:2 errors before review); ties use listed order. Class-positive at >= threshold. Confidence is absolute distance from threshold in chosen operating space.
search.formula: Refit accepted recall 0.70, alpha 0.50 using production weighting and voted decisions (positive only if positive weighted confidence exceeds negative; retain production tie rule). Confidence is the winning weighted confidence. For normalized margins use absolute signed logit distance from each voter cut (same epsilon as linear), enforcing the production directional gate on routed evidence. Refit formula weights inside training folds for recall/alpha changes. Isolate log-odds margin with baseline weights fixed. Test one factor at a time: recall 0.60/0.80 or alpha 0.25/0.75 on original margins. Six mandatory configurations including reference; four optional corner combinations (recall by alpha) on original margins. No class-probability threshold search for formula.
search.linear: Three clipped logit signals, epsilon 1e-6. Stage 1/3: logit(p)-logit(recall-0.70 cut). Routed: logit(r)-logit(b), r=1-confidence for pass1 and confidence for pass2 as recovered from the allowed transformed score and b; zero on defer. Full-batch L-BFGS-B, slopes >=0, free intercept; mean unweighted log-loss + lambda/2 * sum(slopes^2). Lambda in [0.001,0.01,0.1,1], zero initialization, maxiter 500, projected-gradient tolerance 1e-6, ftol 1e-12; solver must report success. Compare identity and inner-cross-fitted sigmoid correction by inner log-loss; retain identity on a tie. Four penalty configurations per partition; calibration and class/cut selection reuse their OOF scores. Conditional route variant at the same four lambdas with extra penalty sum((route slope-global slope)^2)/2; require nonnegative total route slopes. One shared intercept. Fit global anchor first, freeze it, then fit state slopes with the same ridge penalty plus the stated shrinkage penalty. Report 500 coefficient bootstrap refits only for the retained specification on pooled training data; no reselection in that descriptive interval.
search.meta: Use MetaXGBEstimator.suggest and frozen MetaXGBSearchSpace from Step 2A branch 7476e878. Keep balanced weights. Reuse the same 12 distinct seeded random proposals for both objectives; rank once by historical F2 at 0.5 on all rows and once by unweighted log-loss. Reuse predictions across objectives and operating-space choices. Compare each winner in raw vs fold-gated isotonic probability space (existing ECE gate). At most 12 unique tree configurations plus one refit of each distinct winner. Tree search has seven dimensions; linear uses four deterministic penalties. Record sampled parameters and time. Use Optuna RandomSampler(seed=42), sequential non-pruned proposals, stop after 12 unique proposals or 24 attempts. Refit the accepted Meta hyperparameters as one additional descriptive reference. They were historically selected on the full training split; exclude them from the primary inner search unless independently drawn.
search.conditional: Apply diagnostic triggers independently inside each outer training partition using inner OOF evidence. Global Commit 3 summaries are descriptive. Exclude outer labels and predictions from activation. For route reliability, require >=20 per class in each compared state and absolute between-state voter calibration slope difference >=0.5 with the same ordering in at least two of three inner folds. Only then enable shrunk route coefficients. Enable four joint formula corners only if both a one-factor recall change and a one-factor alpha change improve inner loss by >=0.005 each. Enable one cross-fitted rule-evidence ablation only if fit-sample minus cross-fitted precision >=0.05 at >=100 routed observations in two inner folds. Unavailable leakage-safe evidence: defer that ablation; no upstream refit during screening.
search.holdout: Commit 5 only: one stratified 20% holdout of training rows, seed 4305, black-box upstream first with accepted parameters. Lock models and cuts before holdout inspection. Expand once to GLASS if same-row full-refit vs fold-average absolute coverage difference >=0.05, either class retention difference >=0.05, absolute mean loss difference >=0.005, or a GLASS-specific rule-evidence question remains necessary for adoption. Otherwise stop after black-box and identify the unmeasured GLASS shift. Freeze black-box results before expanding; use neither holdout for retuning. The last trigger requires a retained GLASS candidate and either missing valid cross-fitted rule evidence or a >=0.05 rule-rate discrepancy meeting the registered support trigger. One upstream experiment per arm; report costs and isolate meta refit effects.

stability: Report the five outer-fold loss differences and their unweighted sample SD. Evaluate the paired mean and margins on the pooled row-weighted OOF population. Report elapsed time, threads, trial order, failures, parameters, seeds and fold identities.
nesting: Step 2C: common five outer folds using accepted shared fold IDs, three stratified inner folds (shuffle, seed 42). Preserve upstream ten-fold Stage 1 and five-fold Stage 2/3 columns. Fit every learned Stage 4 quantity on the appropriate training partition; use subfold cross-fitting (three stratified folds, seed 43) for supervised transformations and calibration of inner validation predictions. Select one procedure per registered arm, not the best outer variant. Evaluate its locked rule once per outer fold. Pool aligned outer predictions and report each fold. Optimism = outer achieved loss minus selected inner OOF loss, aggregated with outer row weights. No warm starts or deployment-cut retuning on outer scores. Frozen upstream fits can include labels of other Stage 4 outer rows. PR 44 owns upstream nested selection, PR 45 adoption and PR 49 temporal/repeated-split evaluation.
